title: Mate invertibility for a normalized uniformizer square
statement: For the data of the uniformizer quotient and any full-unit-normalized RestrictionSquare supplied by lem-diagonal-uniformizer-restriction-square, the scalar mate of that square is an isomorphism at every unbounded integral derived object K on X.

proof.text: After exact restriction of coefficients, compute the mate on the two-term finite-free resolution. It is invertible on each free term, hence on the cone by the triangulated comparison theorem. Conservativity of exact restriction reflects the isomorphism back to the original mate for every complex.

mathlib_searches.results: Existing declarations provide the finite perfect-model and universal-unit APIs, but no concrete quotient square theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonal_uniformizer_restriction_mate_isIso
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l)
    (π : PadicAlgCl.integers l E)
    (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers l E)) (n : ℕ)
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (R : DiagonalRightDerived
      (CondensedRing.lowerStar (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} l E.1) f))
    (square : RestrictionSquare (quotientMap l E π n) f R
      (canonicalDiagonalRightDerived
        (CondensedRing.lowerStar
          (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} (completedResidue l E π n)) f))) :
    ∀ K : DerivedCategory
      (Modules (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} l E.1) X),
      IsIso ((square.mate (quotientMap l E π n)).app K)
